claim: run_blocking_sql waits for a slot with `async with asyncio.timeout(WORKER_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S)` around `slot.acquire()` and catches the builtin `TimeoutError`; this requires `asyncio.timeout` to exist on every supported Python (3.11+) and to raise an exception the bare `except TimeoutError` catches when the deadline passes, while an external cancellation propagates as CancelledError rather than TimeoutError.
verify_against: Python 3.11/3.12 asyncio.timeouts.Timeout.__aexit__ and pyproject.toml requires-python
verify_hint: Check `asyncio.timeouts.Timeout.__aexit__` in CPython 3.11 and 3.12 (it converts its own CancelledError into TimeoutError only when the deadline fired) and `requires-python` in pyproject.toml.

claim: The comment asserts that on Python 3.11 `asyncio.wait_for` returns a semaphore slot granted in the same tick as a cancellation (so a cancelled call would run), and implies the `asyncio.timeout` + `slot.acquire()` form used instead does not.
source_excerpt:
# Not asyncio.wait_for: on 3.11 it returns a slot granted in the same
        # tick as a cancellation, so a cancelled call would run anyway.
verify_against: CPython 3.11 asyncio.tasks.wait_for and asyncio.locks.Semaphore.acquire
verify_hint: Trace the input: a waiting call whose Semaphore waiter future is resolved by `slot.release()` and whose task is cancelled in the same loop tick; check 3.11 `asyncio.tasks.wait_for` (the `fut.done()` branch on CancelledError that returns the result) versus `Semaphore.acquire`'s CancelledError handler on 3.11 and 3.12 (does it give the granted slot back and wake the next waiter).

claim: When a task blocked in `asyncio.Semaphore.acquire()` inside `asyncio.timeout` is granted the slot and cancelled in the same tick, `acquire` raises CancelledError and returns the slot to the semaphore (so `slot.locked()` is False afterwards and the call is never submitted), on both Python 3.11 and 3.12.
verify_against: CPython 3.11 and 3.12 asyncio/locks.py Semaphore.acquire and _wake_up_next
verify_hint: Check `Semaphore.acquire` in asyncio/locks.py for 3.11 (latest patch) and 3.12: the `except exceptions.CancelledError` branch and whether it increments `_value`/wakes the next waiter when the waiter future was already resolved.
